$comment: What the Weaver's fold does to the graph, as every implementation of the Weaver must do it: a history of recorded events, and the graph it leaves. Every Weaver runs every case, in whatever language it is written. `history` is the events as the Weaver is given them, in the order they are delivered, each as the bus carries a recorded event (a StoredEventResponse, with the payload the bus registry names for its channel): an event that appears twice is delivered twice. `graph` is what the graph then holds, as a store answers it: its `resources` and its `annotations` (each as the graph's annotation codec says the graph holds it, which is not all a view holds). Resources, annotations and a resource's entity types are sets: no order of theirs is stated. `applied` is, for each resource, the last event of its log the Weaver has taken, which it also signals on `weave:applied`: a Weaver follows the record (docs/protocol/TRANSPORT-CONTRACT.md § What repairs a passing frame), and an event the graph cannot take as recorded is taken as nothing. `refused` is how many such events there were, where there are any. The graph says what the record says: a resource's date and an updated annotation's `modified` are the moments their events were recorded, and who a thing is by is who its event records, so that a check of the graph against the record's views finds nothing to repair in a graph the fold has just built. What a rebuild, a catch-up and a reconcile do are not here: they are the service's, and its suite's. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: a created resource is in the graph as its event records it: named and typed by the payload, dated when the event was recorded and not when it was applied, and by the parties the record derived, here the one that asked and the software that did the work

a created event that records no attribution is refused, as an annotation with no creator is: the graph derives none from who sent the event, the resource is not in the graph, and nothing is applied for it
the same event delivered twice is applied once
archiving and unarchiving set the one flag, and the last one stands

an added annotation is by the creator its event records, who asked for it, and not by the party that sent the event, which did the work; the software that made it is kept as its generator, and who it is attributed to is the views' to keep
an annotation added twice is in the graph once, under the id its event gave it
an annotation recorded with no creator is refused: the graph makes none up, and the event is taken as nothing, and counted
a refused event is refused alone: of three annotations added in one burst, the one with no creator is not applied, the two beside it are, and the resource's log is taken past all three
a removed annotation is gone, and removing one that is not there changes nothing
a link added to an annotation's body after it was made is held and read back, and the annotation is dated as changed when the record says the body was
body operations apply in order to what the graph holds: a tag and a link added, then the link removed, leave the tag; the last change dates the annotation
a replaced link is the new one alone; an item added again is there once
a comment's text added to a body is not the graph's to hold: the body is as it was, and the annotation is still dated as changed
a resource's entity tags are a set: one added twice is there once, and one removed is gone
events of different resources reach the graph in no fixed order: a link applied before the resource it points at ends as the same graph
a link to a resource the graph is never given is still the annotation's link, and its target is no resource of the graph's
